title: Reduced vertebrate diversity following feral swine invasions
note: Forest sites invaded by feral swine showed lower native vertebrate diversity, with the effect holding across patches of every size.

title: Population size estimates of invasive wild pigs in the United States
note: National estimates of historical, current, and potential U.S. wild pig populations, documenting a steep upward trend and large areas of unfilled habitat.

title: Hunting as the main technique used to control wild pigs in Brazil
note: A survey of wild pig control in Brazil found hunting is the dominant method, carried out mostly by volunteers and often outside legal channels.

title: Effectiveness of a bounty program for reducing wild pig densities
note: A bounty program failed to reduce wild pig numbers, with densities rising during the program, evidence that bounties are not an effective control tool.

title: Hog Heaven? Challenges of managing introduced wild pigs in natural areas
note: A review of the impacts of wild pigs in natural areas, the traits that make them hard to remove, and what effective control and eradication require.

title: Biotic and abiotic factors predicting the global distribution of wild pigs
note: Combining 129 global density estimates, the study shows that biotic factors like agriculture and vegetation sharply improve predictions of wild pig distribution and density.

title: Interpreting and predicting the spread of invasive wild pigs
note: A three-decade model found U.S. wild pig spread accelerated from about 6.5 to 12.6 km per year, driven by climate-matched expansion plus human-assisted jumps.

title: Anthropogenic factors predict movement of an invasive species
note: Evidence that human activity, not natural dispersal, drives most wild pig range expansion, so movement by people is the spread risk to manage.

title: Wild boar populations up, hunter numbers down: trends in Europe
note: Across 18 European countries, wild boar harvests rose steadily while hunter numbers stalled, indicating recreational hunting alone cannot contain population growth.

title: Consequences of the recent range expansion of nonnative feral swine
note: A foundational overview of feral swine's rapid U.S. range expansion and the resulting risks to crops, native species, and animal and human health.

title: Estimation of the Number of Wild Pigs Found in the United States
keywords: national population estimate, abundance, state-by-state compilation
note: A state-by-state compilation putting the U.S. wild pig population at a mean of roughly 6.3 million animals, within a defensible range of 4.4 to 11.3 million. Ten states account for 99% of the total, and Texas alone for 41%.

title: Evaluation of continuous-catch doors for trapping wild pigs

title: Reproduction in wild pigs subjected to lethal control

title: High hunting pressure selects for earlier birth date in wild boar
